teaser.text: D. R. Horton builds homes, chiefly to sell them to households, and also develops rental communities and related services. A dollar enters when a buyer, tenant, investor, or builder pays, and it leaves first for land, construction, labor, financing, and the costs of completing the transaction.

stock.title: D.R. Horton stock forecast
stock.meta_description: D.R. Horton’s stock forecast weighs bear, base and bull scenarios, margins, cash conversion and today’s valuation.
stock.opening: D.R. Horton’s weighted scenario reaches $212.12 by October 2029, with 30% bear, 55% base and 15% bull probabilities. It hinges on margins recovering, inventory turning faster and cash supporting the capital plan.
stock.closing: The full memo also answers what D.R. Horton’s business does, how its rivals compare, how management allocates capital and what risks shape the outlook.

blocks.heading: Where could D.R. Horton’s shares go?

paragraphs.text: The forecast points to limited near-term upside but a substantial possible gain by October 2029. The weighted price is $129.76 in October 2027, a 4% loss with dividends. It rises to $161.63 in October 2028, a 21% return. By October 2029, it reaches $212.12, a 59% return. The bear case ends at $79.04 in 2029. The bull case ends at $426.33. Today’s price is $136.84.
The bear case has 30% probability. The base case has 55%, and the bull case 15%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for D.R. Horton, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: Normal operating profit rises in the base case from $4,200M in October 2027 to $4,700M in October 2028. It reaches $5,300M in 2029. The bear path falls to $3,400M and then $3,000M. It recovers to $3,200M by 2029. The bull path starts at $5,000M and reaches $6,100M. It reaches $6,900M in 2029. The June quarter posted a 12.5% operating margin, while home-sales gross margin was 20.7%. Operating income averaged $5,870.2M across 2021–25 but fell to $4,424.2M in 2025. Communities rose 9% while orders stayed broadly flat. That implies about 8% lower orders per community.

blocks.heading: How much cash does D.R. Horton really make?

paragraphs.text: The conventional property-and-equipment figure was $137.4 million, but that is not the full investment needed to keep a homebuilder supplied. Deducting stated stock compensation of $131.0 million from operating cash gives $3,116.7 million before capital expenditure and other adjustments. A specialist therefore tests cash over several years, including replacement land spending and inventory write-offs.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for D.R. Horton today?

paragraphs.text: At $136.84 a share on October 19, 2026, D.R. Horton’s valuation depends on how much of its recent profit can last. The market value of all its shares is US$38,274.3 million, while enterprise value is US$41,750.5 million. Market value belongs to shareholders; enterprise value estimates the cost of owning the operating business by adding debt and subtracting cash. The difference is US$3,476.2 million.

blocks.heading: How much does D.R. Horton pay per share?

paragraphs.text: Base dividends rise to $1.80 in 2027 and $1.95 in 2028. They reach $2.10 in 2029. The bear case holds DPS at $1.60. The bull case pays $1.90 and then $2.25. It reaches $2.65. Fiscal 2025 DPS was $1.60, and fiscal 2026 guidance included $500M of dividend payments. The base path therefore slows the historical growth rate without assuming a cut.

blocks.heading: Does D.R. Horton's cash cover its dividend?

paragraphs.text: DHI’s weighted price can reach $212.12 by October 2029 if margins recover, inventory turns faster and cash supports the capital plan. July guidance calls for fiscal 2026 revenue of $32.5–33.0 billion and 83,800–84,300 homebuilding closings. Fourth-quarter home-sales gross margin is guided at 20.5%–21%. Management also expects at least $3,000 million of fiscal 2026 operating cash. On September 15, it raised expected repurchases to at least $3.25 billion; dividend-payment guidance is $500 million.

In 2025, operating cash excluding Financial Services recovered to $3,247.7 million from $1,908.2 million. Construction in progress and finished homes released $1,228.8 million, while residential land and lots absorbed $1,884.3 million. The company was selling through one stage while funding the next.

blocks.heading: What could change D.R. Horton's dividend?

paragraphs.text: September 2026 results, due before the market opens on October 29, will test the reduced closing and revenue outlook against margins, earnings and cash generation. Orders per community, cancellations, incentives and realized margins will show whether demand improves. Fiscal 2027 will carry a full year without the energy-efficient-home credit for homes acquired after June 30, 2026. Buybacks, dividends, land spending and debt reduction compete for operating cash.

blocks.heading: Did D.R. Horton keep its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Management’s forecast record is mixed. On October 29, 2024, it predicted 90,000–92,000 home closings for fiscal 2025 and approximately US$2.4 billion of repurchases. Horton closed 84,863 homes for fiscal 2025, below the forecast range, while repurchases exceeded the original plan. As of October 19, 2026, Horton’s latest fiscal 2026 repurchase expectation was at least US$3.25 billion.

blocks.heading: What are D.R. Horton’s last eight quarters of revenue and profit?

paragraphs.text: Over the last eight reported quarters through June 2026, Horton beat estimates five times. That record shows recent execution, but it cannot make customers close on homes. October’s report must put revenue, total profit, margins and cash beside EPS.
